{
  "rules": [
    "If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.",
    "If sentiment is negative (≤0.0) and forecast is trending downward, increase forecast slope to avoid underreaction.",
    "When true outcome shows sharp downward spike after a peak, model often overcorrects — reduce forecast peak height by 5–10%.",
    "If model forecast is consistently above true outcome over 3–5 days, apply mean reversion: subtract 1–2% per day from forecast.",
    "If sentiment is high (≥0.4) and forecast is flat, expect volatility — increase forecast range by ±2–3% to account for sentiment-driven noise.",
    "If forecast is rising steadily but true outcome shows early mean reversion, pause forecast growth for 1–2 days before resuming.",
    "When sentiment is low and true outcome is rising, model often underestimates — add 1–2% to forecast to capture sentiment lag."
  ]
}
